name: client_inside
title: Inside the transport-v2 client
summary: Three entry points drive one client transport: the yume command, the optional desktop app through yume_facade, and the experimental C ABI through yume_embed. The transport carries streams over authenticated tunnels to yumed.
comment: cmake/YumeLayering.cmake enforces that the C ABI never links the desktop layer. Keep the notes in step with docs/SOURCE_MAP.md.

nodes.title: YUME CLI
nodes.note: The yume command parses flags and the config file, then runs the connected client in its own process.

nodes.title: DESKTOP APP
nodes.note: The optional desktop app drives the client through yume_facade, which adds session objects, a traffic meter and key management on top of yume_embed.

nodes.title: C ABI
nodes.note: The opt-in C interface for other programs. It reaches transport v2 only through yume_embed, never the desktop layer, and it is build-tree only and not frozen.

nodes.title: CLIENT TRANSPORT
nodes.note: The transport core owns frame dispatch, write scheduling and flow credit for every stream, whichever entry point started it.

nodes.title: TUNNEL POOL
nodes.note: Holds the authenticated tunnels to yumed. Each new SOCKS session is bound to one live tunnel for its lifetime, so its stream numbers stay on one TLS connection.
